topic.title: Environment: A school teaches children to save animals
topic.focus: A school teaches children to save animals

candidate_instructions: Read all five sections. Answer Questions 1-5. Follow the stated word limits exactly.

sections.heading: Animals are disappearing
sections.text: In 2013, a school in Borneo sees that animals are disappearing. The forest is getting smaller. Many animals have no home. The school wants to help save the animals. The teachers and children make a plan.

sections.heading: Learning about animals
sections.text: Teachers teach children about each animal. They learn about orangutans, birds, and snakes. They learn where these animals live. They learn what animals need to survive. The children love these lessons. They understand why animals are important.

sections.heading: Planting trees
sections.text: The school plants trees to make a forest again. Every child plants at least 10 trees a year. The forest grows back slowly. Small animals return. Birds come to live in the trees. Insects live in the soil.

sections.heading: Visiting the young forest
sections.text: After three years, the young forest is 50,000 trees big. Classes go to the forest to study. They see animals living there. They count birds. They find insects. Children understand that their work makes a real difference.

sections.heading: Protecting the future
sections.text: Now 500 children plant trees every year. The forest grows bigger and stronger. More animals come back. The school is an example for other schools. They say if children love nature, they will protect it. The animals have hope.

passage.full_text:
Paragraph 1 — Animals are disappearing
In 2013, a school in Borneo sees that animals are disappearing. The forest is getting smaller. Many animals have no home. The school wants to help save the animals. The teachers and children make a plan.

Paragraph 2 — Learning about animals
Teachers teach children about each animal. They learn about orangutans, birds, and snakes. They learn where these animals live. They learn what animals need to survive. The children love these lessons. They understand why animals are important.

Paragraph 3 — Planting trees
The school plants trees to make a forest again. Every child plants at least 10 trees a year. The forest grows back slowly. Small animals return. Birds come to live in the trees. Insects live in the soil.

Paragraph 4 — Visiting the young forest
After three years, the young forest is 50,000 trees big. Classes go to the forest to study. They see animals living there. They count birds. They find insects. Children understand that their work makes a real difference.

Paragraph 5 — Protecting the future
Now 500 children plant trees every year. The forest grows bigger and stronger. More animals come back. The school is an example for other schools. They say if children love nature, they will protect it. The animals have hope.
